title: How a C# program works — interview

items.question: How is C# different from TypeScript at run time?
items.answer: C# compiles to Intermediate Language (IL) with Common Type System (CTS) metadata, and the Common Language Runtime (CLR) enforces types at run time. TypeScript is a compile-time checker that emits JavaScript — the engine never sees those types. A Node.js Lambda and a .NET Lambda may both receive the same JSON event, but they run on completely different hosts with different type systems.
followUps: Where does the Common Type System sit relative to the C# language?
What does dotnet build produce that tsc does not?
items.sixtySeconds: C# keeps real types in the assembly. TypeScript erases them. CLR versus V8. Same AWS event, different process and type enforcement.

items.question: Walk through source to CPU for a typical worker.
items.answer: You write .cs files. The Roslyn compiler emits IL into a .dll assembly with metadata. At run time the CLR's Just-In-Time (JIT) compiler turns each method into native machine code (with tiered optimization). Alternatively, Native Ahead-of-Time (AOT) compiles everything to a native binary before deployment. This is fundamentally different from running node file.js.
followUps: Is a .NET assembly the same as an ES module?
items.sixtySeconds: Source → IL assembly → JIT at run time, or AOT to native binary. An assembly is a versioned metadata unit, not a JavaScript import graph.

items.question: How do you choose the C# language version?
items.answer: It follows the Target Framework Moniker (TFM). net10.0 means C# 14 by default. Override LangVersion only when you have a deliberate reason — never use latest, because that tracks whichever compiler is installed and breaks reproducibility across build machines.
followUps: How do you print the compiler's chosen version?
items.sixtySeconds: TFM selects LangVersion. Pin the TFM, not latest. Implicit usings are auto-generated global using statements for common namespaces.

items.question: What is the entry point of a new console app?
items.answer: Top-level statements in a single file — the default dotnet new console template. The compiler synthesizes a static Main method behind the scenes. The classic form (static int Main(string[] args)) is equivalent. Only one file per project may have top-level statements. args is a string[] of command-line arguments.
followUps: Can file-based apps use Main instead of top-level statements?
What happens if you use await at the top level?
items.sixtySeconds: One entry per executable: top-level statements or explicit Main. The compiler generates the rest. args is the command-line argument array.

items.question: What is a file-based app in .NET 10?
items.answer: A single .cs file you run with dotnet run file.cs — no .csproj on disk. C# 14 #: directives configure packages, properties, and SDK inline (like a virtual project file). Use for quick scripts and spikes. Convert to a real project with dotnet project convert when it grows. Native AOT publish is on by default; disable it if you need reflection.
items.sixtySeconds: C# 14 / .NET 10: dotnet run file.cs, #: directives for inline config, convert to project when it outgrows one file.
